speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping and waking up frightened. To help you, can you tell me if these episodes happen every night or just occasionally?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since she wakes up frightened, screams, but is immediately alert and consolable with no memory of the event, does she ever sit up in bed or kick out during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your report of yelling, crying, and a complete lack of memory for the events the next day, which distinguishes this from nightmares, do you notice if she has trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night?
